_doc: One file per place; see places_build.py. Amounts in Kenyan shillings. The debt component, history and facts are refreshed by pipeline/fetch_kenya.py from the National Treasury's Quarterly Economic and Budgetary Review (needs pypdf); edit wording here, not numbers.
name: Kenya
publisher: National Treasury and Economic Planning, Kenya
title: Kenya Debt Clock: Live Public and Publicly Guaranteed Debt, Official Data
headline: public and publicly guaranteed debt
link_label: public and publicly guaranteed debt, KSh
subject: The Government of Kenya
sum_note: Kenya's public and publicly guaranteed debt (gross; domestic and external), quarter-end, from the National Treasury's Quarterly Economic and Budgetary Review.
scope_note: This is the "total public and publicly guaranteed debt" that Kenya's National Treasury states in its Quarterly Economic and Budgetary Review: the national government's external and domestic debt at the end of the quarter, in Kenyan shillings, plus debt the government has guaranteed. It is gross: the Treasury's separate net figure, which subtracts deposits, is lower. County governments' own borrowing is not included. The newest quarter in the report is provisional.
trend_why: We use the change over the latest twelve months rather than the last quarter because quarterly changes swing with the exchange rate and with issuance.
legend: Kenya's public debt is reported quarterly, at quarter-end. Issuance happens in lumps at auctions and maturities, so the live number is a straight-line projection between official figures, shown here next to them.
cadence: Quarterly. The National Treasury publishes a Quarterly Economic and Budgetary Review about six weeks after each quarter ends.
after_text: , about six weeks after each quarter-end
next_update: The National Treasury publishes a Quarterly Economic and Budgetary Review about six weeks after each quarter ends; this page re-bases to it automatically on the next daily build after it appears.

extra_sources.name: Central Bank of Kenya, Public debt

notes: Why the Treasury's review: it is the National Treasury's own quarterly statement of the debt. The fetcher reads the table with nine consecutive quarter-ends and checks that domestic plus external equals the grand total.
Gross: the Treasury also reports net debt (after deposits); the gross figure is used here.
Provisional: the newest quarter in each report is marked provisional and may be revised in the next review.

Currency: Kenyan shillings. The World Debt Clock converts them to US dollars at the US Treasury's Reporting Rates of Exchange (a quarterly official rate as of 30 September 2026; the page for the World Debt Clock shows the rate and its date).
